def factor_path_efficiency_tail_mean_smooth(df):
    """Reward persistent directional price paths while using a smoother downside-fragility modifier."""
    df_copy = df.copy()
    close = df_copy["close"].replace(0.0, np.nan)
    net_move = close - close.shift(126)
    path_length = close.diff().abs().rolling(126, min_periods=126).sum()
    efficiency = net_move / path_length.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    recent_move = close - close.shift(63)
    recent_length = close.diff().abs().rolling(63, min_periods=63).sum()
    recent_efficiency = recent_move / recent_length.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    ret = close / close.shift(1) - 1.0
    downside_pressure = (-ret.clip(upper=0.0)).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
    upside_pressure = ret.clip(lower=0.0).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
    baseline = ret.abs().rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean().clip(lower=1e-6)
    downside_fragility = ((downside_pressure - upside_pressure) / baseline).clip(lower=0.0, upper=2.0)
    signal = efficiency * recent_efficiency.abs() * (1.0 - 0.25 * downside_fragility)
    df_copy["factor_path_efficiency_tail_mean_smooth"] = signal.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    return df_copy["factor_path_efficiency_tail_mean_smooth"]
rationale: Mutates the qualified signed path-efficiency parent by replacing the noisy 20-bar extreme-tail comparison with a 20-bar average downside-versus-upside pressure comparison. This targets the parent's weaker predictive stability metrics by reducing sensitivity to one-off return extremes, while preserving the long-horizon directional efficiency core, recent-efficiency confirmation, bounded risk attenuation, positive payoff evidence, and low-turnover character.
